images.title: Choose a frame or a section
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: a high-fidelity design review image for an existing iPhone football video editor called Power Shot.
Render a square, high-resolution design sheet with exactly TWO upright app screens side by side, front-on, with equal dimensions and generous spacing on a warm light-gray board. The screens must be large and their interface labels crisply readable. No perspective tilt, no hands, no bulky phone hardware. Thin rounded screen silhouette and understated shadow only. Include a small clear sheet title above both screens.
Established app visual system: near-black background, charcoal floating bottom panels, restrained translucent iOS glass, mint-green selection strokes and sliders (#58EFA8), white SF Pro-like typography and muted gray secondary labels. Rounded corners, generous touch targets, disciplined spacing. Use bright yellow-lime only for the export/done accent if needed. This is a practical shippable native iPhone UI mockup, not sci-fi concept art.
Video content: photorealistic source football footage on an outdoor green pitch with white lines, a goal and fence in the distance, one adult player in a dark training shirt and shorts and one real white football. Each timeline thumbnail shows a plausible successive frame of this same shot. Do not add artificial ball skins or glowing ball trails, speed statistics, meters, graphs, scores, or invented physical analysis.
The screen focuses on ONE chosen effect with its own configuration panel. Do not show the existing nine-tile effect grid; keep the football preview big, around the upper half of the screen. The editing timeline must remain visible above effect controls. Single-frame selections are a thin mint playhead and a labeled marker. Range selections are a shaded mint region between TWO distinct draggable bracket handles, with gray footage outside. A small 'Original' preview comparison pill is allowed near the video. Source time labels include milliseconds where precision matters.
All specified labels must be rendered exactly, neatly, without spelling errors. Do not add long explanatory paragraphs inside the app or annotations that obscure its controls. This is a proposed configuration redesign, not an assertion that these settings are already implemented.
Sheet title (verbatim): "01 / CHOOSE WHEN"
LEFT screen: dedicated precise frame picker, header "Choose impact frame" with a small close icon. Large football preview paused at the instant the boot contacts the real ball, a minimal mint target around this small contact area. Under the video, centered play button and a timestamp "00:04.283". A horizontal expanded filmstrip with 7 distinguishable close-up shot thumbnails, with a FIXED central mint playhead; center thumbnail outlined and captioned "Impact". Add a compact overview timeline below this strip showing its small zoomed section within the entire clip. Under it, two large outlined frame-nudge buttons "−1 frame" and "+1 frame" side by side. Tiny helper "Drag to scrub · Pinch to zoom". Bottom full-width mint button "Use this frame". The chosen frame is visibly in the large preview as well as the timeline, not merely a tiny card.
RIGHT screen: dedicated range picker, header "Choose effect range" with a close icon. Same large football preview at early flight, play button. Filmstrip with a clear mint selection spanning several thumbnails, with two strong draggable bracket handles at its start and end and a playhead inside. Beneath it: two equally prominent timestamp chips "Start 00:04.100" and "End 00:05.300". Range chip "1.20 s selected". Compact controls "Set start here" and "Set end here". Tiny helper "Drag the ends to trim". Bottom full-width mint button "Use this range". Outside the selected section the footage is gray/unhighlighted, making it visually obvious when the camera effect is active.
Board captions beneath the screens: "One exact source frame" and "A section of the source video".

Sheet title (verbatim): "02 / FOLLOW & IMPACT"
Both editor screens have a top bar with back chevron, "POWER SHOT", and a small mint export icon. A big preview, a play button, an "Original" comparison pill, and one compact configuration panel.
LEFT selected effect: "Ball Follow". Show the real ball near the crop center during its flight, thin white safe-crop corners over the preview. Visible filmstrip timeline with mint selected range and separate start/end bracket handles, range labels "04.10" and "05.30". Bottom panel title "Ball Follow" with a discreet down chevron to switch effect. A timing row "Follow section" with "Edit range". Two clear parameter rows: "Zoom" with a slider and value "1.8×"; "Follow motion" with two segmented options "Smooth" (mint selected) and "Tight". A compact "Framing" row with "Auto ball" selected and "Adjust crop" alternate. Do not add generic 'Strength'.
RIGHT selected effect: "Impact Zoom". Preview paused at a boot and ball strike, with a small draggable mint rounded target box around the contact area. Visible filmstrip with a single labeled mint diamond "Impact" at "00:04.283" and a narrow softly shaded effect window around it; this is a moment-centered effect, not an arbitrary long selected range. Panel title "Impact Zoom". Timing row "Impact frame" with timestamp "00:04.283" and "Change". Parameter "Zoom" slider value "2.0×". Parameter "Zoom duration" slider value "0.45 s". Segmented "Motion" options "Soft" and "Punchy" (selected mint). Small helper immediately under preview: "Drag target · Pinch to zoom". No unrelated controls.
Board captions: "Choose where the camera follows" and "Choose the moment and the punch".

Sheet title (verbatim): "03 / TIME & ROTATION"
Both editor screens have back chevron, "POWER SHOT", mint export icon, a big source-footage preview, a play button and "Original".
LEFT selected effect: "Speed Ramp". Video paused just after boot contact, with a small restrained badge "¼ speed" in one corner. Timeline has clear start/end draggable bracket handles around a highlighted slow-motion section; original footage gray outside. Show the same outdoor football frame with a very subtle 3-degree image rotation and a fine unobtrusive horizon/angle guide near a lower corner, no extreme Dutch angle. Timeline has a single mint marker "Impact" and "00:04.283". Config panel title "Tilt Punch". "Impact frame" timestamp with "Change". Parameter "Angle" slider value "3°". "Direction" segmented controls "Left" (selected mint) and "Right" with simple curved-arrow icons. Parameter "Settle time" slider value "0.40 s". Footer "Preview punch". Keep the target video physically plausible, subtle rotation, no artificial ball effects.
Board captions: "Control the slow-motion section" and "Control angle and recovery".

Sheet title (verbatim): "05 / FREEZE & FRAME REVIEW"
Both editor screens have a back chevron, "POWER SHOT" top title, a big readable football preview and compact contextual controls.
LEFT selected effect: "Freeze + Path". Preview paused at contact. Draw a thin mint observed two-dimensional ball path curving gently toward the goal over the video, no neon ball replacement and no real-world measurements. Timeline shows one chosen source-frame marker "Freeze" at "00:04.283" and an attached clearly distinct inserted hold chip "Hold 0.70 s", rather than making the hold look like an ordinary section of source video. Config panel title "Freeze + Path". Timing row "Freeze frame" with "00:04.283" and "Change". "Hold duration" slider value "0.70 s". Two separate native switch rows "Show path" ON and "Initial direction" ON. A compact row "Path ends" with "End of tracked flight" and a small edit icon. Button "Preview freeze". This distinguishes choosing the frozen source frame from choosing the added pause length.
RIGHT selected effect: "Frame Steps". Big preview paused at an early airborne football moment. Beneath, an elegant horizontal strip of THREE user-selected source-frame cards: "01 Contact", "02 Flight" (mint selected outline), "03 Finish", plus a small "+ Add" tile. Each card must show the SAME scene at a different plausible moment and the selected "02 Flight" card must match the large preview. Below this curated strip is a precision timeline filmstrip with fixed mint center playhead and readout "00:04.533"; compact overview scrubber and generous "−1 frame" / "+1 frame" buttons. Bottom panel title "Frame Steps". Actions "Update selected frame" (primary mint) and "Remove" (quiet secondary). Small subtle line "For frame review". No export montage, three-frame movie or claim that these cards burn into the export. Source frames are chosen individually rather than hardcoded +0.25/+0.50 automatic choices.
Board captions: "Choose the frame, then the hold" and "Build your own review sequence".
